King Chung (Johnny) Ho

“Don't just aspire to make a living; aspire to make a difference.”

I'm an applied AI/ML researcher and engineer. Most of my work is machine learning that has to hold up outside the lab, where labels are scarce, data arrives messy from many sites, and the people affected by a model's output are patients.

Today I'm a Senior Principal AI Engineer and tech lead at Edwards Lifesciences, where my team builds the imaging platform and image foundation models behind AI-assisted medical imaging. Before that I spent five years at Verily (Google Life Sciences) training multimodal foundation models on more than 1.6 million hours of wearable sensor data. I did my Ph.D. at UCLA on deep learning for stroke imaging.

I keep up with the research frontier by building things myself. My current independent project is an agent for competitive Pokémon battles that combines imitation learning, search and reinforcement learning: a small lab for questions about planning when much of the game state is hidden. I write about it on the blog.

Experience

  1. Edwards Lifesciences

    Jun 2026 – Present

    Senior Principal AI Engineer, Machine Learning (Tech Lead) · Irvine, CA

    • Technical owner of the end-to-end AI imaging platform; lead a six-person AI/ML team across data, foundation models and production AI systems.
    • Architected and launched an AI-assisted image annotation platform that cut expert annotation time by 50%, and lead the production batch-inference system designed to scale to millions of DICOM images.
    • Lead CT anatomical localization built on image foundation models (e.g., Merlin) and few-shot learning for limited-label regimes, reaching < 3 mm localization error against expert annotations.

  2. Verily (Google Life Sciences)

    Jan 2021 – May 2026

    Senior Data Scientist, Machine Learning (Tech Lead) · Los Angeles, CA

    • Tech lead of a three-person ML team, owning foundation-model development end to end on multi-terabyte longitudinal wearable datasets from studies in the U.S., Europe and Asia.
    • Built multimodal self-supervised foundation models on 1.6M+ hours of wearable sensor data (PPG, accelerometer, gyroscope); the embeddings improved AUROC by 10% on average across 20+ downstream tasks. Extended multimodal vision transformers to combine sensor modalities with text.
    • Made Vertex AI training 5× faster, built cross-partner Dataflow harmonization pipelines, and co-authored 5 Nature Portfolio papers and 3 patents.

    • Led ML development for next-generation AI features on the core survey platform; deployed 6 production ML models.
    • Built survey completion-rate and completion-time prediction models, improving prediction by 10%+ across key customer segments.
    • Granted patent (US 12,141,663 B2) and the SurveyMonkey Patent Award.
